record.title: Make the Apps page look like an app store
record.description: The Apps page is now a store-style list: a header, one card per app with icon, name, category, tagline, description, honest facts and a single Open button, and the install how-to below. The outdated Preview button and the empty Feedback dialog were removed, and the preview posters are no longer advertised to search engines. Checked live in desktop Chrome and at phone widths; not checked on a real phone.

content.summary: The Apps page is now a store-style list: a header, one card per app with icon, name, category, tagline, description, honest facts and a single Open button, and the install how-to below. The outdated Preview button and the empty Feedback dialog were removed, and the preview posters are no longer advertised to search engines. Checked live in desktop Chrome and at phone widths; not checked on a real phone.
content.objective: Present the apps professionally using only what is true and current.
acceptance_criteria: Each app shows its icon, name, category, tagline, description, availability and a single Open action.
No outdated previews, empty feedback dialog, ratings, counts or prices appear.
Cards sit side by side on desktop and stack on phones without horizontal overflow.
The page stays within its JavaScript budget and the visual and end-to-end checks pass.
discoveries: Windows and Linux wrap phone-width text differently, so one Android capture has a documented wider height tolerance in the visual check.
next_actions: Look at the page on a real phone once.
Add fresh screenshots later if wanted; none were kept because the old previews were outdated.

record.title: Add a bot check to the sign-in, sign-up and reset forms
record.description: Add a bot check to the account forms before public launch, using a free provider that the account backend supports natively.

content.summary: Add a bot check to the account forms before public launch, using a free provider that the account backend supports natively.
content.objective: Keep automated abuse out of the account forms without adding friction for most people.
acceptance_criteria: The sign-in, sign-up and reset forms show the provider widget and send its result with each request.
The account backend verifies the result and rejects requests without a valid one.
The forms stay usable on narrow screens and with keyboard-only input.
Turning the check on is a separate, approved provider-settings step with a rollback.
next_actions: Create the provider widget for the account site and record its public site identifier.
Add the widget to the three forms in one reviewed change, behind the provider-settings step.
Verify sign-in, sign-up and reset end to end on a phone and a desktop browser.
blockers: Needs a captcha provider account and its site key and secret, and the account backend's captcha setting switched on. Those are credentials and a provider setting only the owner can create.

record.title: Check the account pages and project boards on a real phone
record.description: The account pages and the public project boards were checked on a real phone on 2026-11-13: nothing looked off. Reported by the owner; not independently observed.

content.summary: The account pages and the public project boards were checked on a real phone on 2026-11-13: nothing looked off. Reported by the owner; not independently observed.
content.objective: Confirm sign-in, sign-out, the account pages and the project boards behave on an actual phone, including the home-screen app.
acceptance_criteria: Sign-in, sign-out and the Fitness handoff work on a real phone.
The four project-board tabs and card details open, scroll and close without layout breaks.
Findings are recorded and any fix ships through the normal reviewed path.
discoveries: Owner report, 2026-11-13: sign-in, sign-out, the four board tabs and the account pages looked right on a phone.
next_actions: Repeat the pass after any large change to the account pages or the boards.

record.title: Show a live online-now count in the site header
record.description: The site header shows how many people are on the website right now, in place of the brand text: a dim dot, then a count once connected. It counts visible site tabs through an anonymous live connection that stores nothing and needs no database change. Checked live in desktop Chrome with two browsers (1, then 2, then 1) and at phone widths; not checked on a real phone. Historical traffic, referrers and per-app counts stay on FW-ANALYTICS-001.

content.summary: The site header shows how many people are on the website right now, in place of the brand text: a dim dot, then a count once connected. It counts visible site tabs through an anonymous live connection that stores nothing and needs no database change. Checked live in desktop Chrome with two browsers (1, then 2, then 1) and at phone widths; not checked on a real phone. Historical traffic, referrers and per-app counts stay on FW-ANALYTICS-001.
content.objective: Give a truthful, privacy-safe live count that never shows a made-up number.
acceptance_criteria: The header shows a dim dot when the count is unknown and a number only for a real positive count.
The count is recomputed from the current presence snapshot and counts each visible tab once.
Nothing identifying is sent or stored, and the privacy page says so.
It runs only on the production site origins and is loaded after the page settles.
The header looks right on a real phone.
discoveries: The channel is public, so anyone with the public key could inflate the number; treat it as a casual indicator.
Realtime connection quotas on the shared project apply; past them the display goes dim.
next_actions: Look at the header on a real phone once.
Decide whether a per-browser count and a traffic view belong to FW-ANALYTICS-001.

record.title: Make Projects owner-only and check it live
record.description: The Projects tab and page are for the signed-in account owner only. The static site ships no board data; a server endpoint verifies the owner and returns every card. The owner signed in on 2026-11-14 and confirmed the Projects tab and boards appear.

content.summary: The Projects tab and page are for the signed-in account owner only. The static site ships no board data; a server endpoint verifies the owner and returns every card. The owner signed in on 2026-11-14 and confirmed the Projects tab and boards appear.
content.objective: Show every project card to the owner and nobody else, without per-card hiding.
acceptance_criteria: Signed-out visitors and every other account see no Projects tab and receive no board data.
The signed-in owner sees the tab and all boards at the account origin.
The built static site contains no board card text.
The owner view is checked on a real device.
discoveries: The owner endpoint needs the server-only owner list setting; without it the page fails closed and shows nothing, for everyone.
Pages on the main site show the Projects link only while a harmless hint cookie set by the account site is present; the account page still verifies the owner on the server.
next_actions: Repeat the check after any change to sign-in or the owner list.
